standard.title: Specification for Side Scuttles for Inland Vessels - Part 1 : General Requirements
standard.sector: Transport Engineering / Inland, Harbour Crafts and Fishing Vessels

sectional_committee.name: Inland, Harbour Crafts and Fishing Vessels Sectional Committee

standard.description: This standard specifies the general requirements, classification, dimensions, materials, and testing schedules for side scuttles (portholes) fitted on inland navigation vessels. These side scuttles are round openings with an area not exceeding 0.16 m² designed to provide daylight, visibility, and watertight/weathertight closure in the hull or superstructure.

certification.description: Voluntary Quality and Performance Specification. Unlike safety-critical builders hardware or pressure cylinders which are under strict statutory Quality Control Orders (QCOs), side scuttles for inland vessels under IS 11294 (Part 1) are certified on a voluntary basis. Manufacturers are eligible to apply for a BIS license to use the Standard Mark (ISI Mark). However, compliance is universally mandated inside all national public sector (such as Inland Waterways Authority of India - IWAI), port authority, and commercial river barge procurement tenders.
requirements: Every certified side scuttle and its packaging box must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) to verify quality compliance.

Side scuttles must be specified as with or without a deadlight. A deadlight is a hinged metal cover that can be clamped watertight over the glass pane to provide double-barrier protection during extreme weather, or in the event of glass breakage.

The main frame, glassholder, and deadlight must be made of high-strength, corrosion-resistant materials suitable for marine service (such as cast steel, brass, bronze, or marine-grade aluminum alloy).

Glass panes must be thermally toughened safety glass satisfying high impact and pressure testing parameters (evaluated via the non-destructive punch testing method of ISO 614) to prevent sudden shattering under wave impact.

Requires robust swing-bolt (eyelet bolt) or toggle arrangements with nuts to apply uniform compression force on the rubber or elastomeric gaskets, ensuring a reliable watertight seal under wave and hydraulic impact.
Specifies standard clear light diameters (nominal sizes) for selection: 200, 250, 300, 350, 400, and 450 mm.
